surfaces.outermost_note: the torus the certificate started from (F_last) is the solver's own check only unless its request comes back verified: the outermost ring drawn is the first of these requests that did
surfaces.how: tori torux.analysis recorded during the solve (torus_record), their sections at phi = 0 from their series, flux_reference minus the loop integral of A of torux.reference.fast64 round the drawn section (2048-point trapezoid)
surfaces.note: for the three inner tori bn_off is the largest |B.n|/|B| of the solve's own acceptance: tori of its continuation, not answers refined to 3e-15 and checked independently. The outermost is such an answer

design_surface.what: the file's outermost stored surface (the request is its flux, by QUASR's definition: the loop integral of A round its own theta curve at phi_s = 0), cut at cylindrical phi = 0 by torux.design.planar_section, drawn dashed, on a channel of paper and over the curve's own, so that it reads as one closed curve all round

branches.what: generating curve u- of the certificate, regrown from its own fundamental domain by torux.barrier.grow_step on the certificate's section without its cut, and its mirror image Su-, the stable branch (stellarator symmetry): unstable solid, stable dashed, drawn in the small view of the whole plane only
branches.note: the regrown pieces above resolved_to_level keep the regrown spacing but not the turning limit at the narrowest lobe tips (the refinement's parameter floor), well below what the inset can show

lost_point_reproduced.what: the certificate's lost line, from its start on the fundamental domain of its branch, one period map at a time (FieldSection.step, the certificate's map): its last point is the lost point, and the next period stops (the line turns, B_phi changes sign)
